the_batch.read_from: the manifest of any run directory it produced
the_batch.runtime_tree: /tmp/claude-0/native/runtime, synced before the D02 audit-report rule landed
the_batch.scope: the eleven target periods whose original is saved - every period a batch can attempt today

visible_in_the_output.not_a_defect_in_the_batch: it ran the rules it was bound to. A batch that showed 95 items here would mean the runtime tree had drifted from the closure its manifests name.
visible_in_the_output.so: the four audit-report blocks the new rule removes are present in this batch's row, which is what a pre-fix closure looks like from the outside. The batch is evidence for the version it ran, not for the current one.
visible_in_the_output.what: Pfizer's D02 public row in this batch begins with 'Evaluation of product liability and other product-related litigation' - block 1881, the heading of the auditor's critical audit matter.

scripts/vnext/historical_text_results.py.effect: a rule file, so the repository now mints a different closure than the batch ran under

not_closure_bound.effect: neither is a rule file, so the report is produced by the current reading layer while the runs it reads were produced under the earlier closure. That is the intended arrangement: a reading fix does not require recomputing what it reads.

what_this_batch_is_and_is_not.is: diagnostic and regression evidence for closure sha256:df2f56ff...; the measurement of what an earlier year delivers; and the material the report layer was checked against.
what_this_batch_is_and_is_not.is_not: acceptance evidence for the current closure. The D02 rule change needs its own targeted verification - one Pfizer coordinate, not a new batch - once the runtime tree is re-synced.

why_this_exists: The review asked that a running batch be saved bound to the version it actually ran, rather than stopped and recomputed every time a report layer problem is found. This records which version that is, in a way a reader can check, before the batch's numbers are reported.
